title: Rerun job submits each workflow run once and runs protect last
answers: approval rerun restarts the same workflow run twice
protect check fails after maintainer approval even though other jobs were rerun
why is protect rerun after the other failed jobs in the auto-rerun
body:
Invariant: several failed jobs can belong to one workflow run, so rows are emitted as `<workflow run databaseId> <job name>` and deduped with `sort -u -k1,1` on the run ID before submitting.
The `protect` job is held back and rerun only after the other reruns are submitted, because it polls the other checks and fails on the first failure it sees.
Non-protect reruns are sent in the background (`rerun "$id" &`), so a bare `wait` must sit between that loop and `rerun "$protect_id"`; removing the `wait` lets protect be submitted before the other reruns have been submitted.
Enforced in .github/workflows/rerun-workflow-run.yml, in the `rows=$(... | sort -u -k1,1)` pipeline, the `protect_id` loop that submits reruns, and the `wait` before `rerun "$protect_id"`.
What breaks if skipped: without -k1,1 a run with two failed jobs is rerun twice; if protect is submitted first, or before `wait`, it can fail on checks that are about to be rerun.
The name must stay last in each row because job names can contain spaces (e.g. `python (1)`).
applies: Row formatting and submission order in the approval rerun workflow only.

says: Approving a rerun triggers duplicate execution of the same workflow run.
Protection check fails immediately after maintainer approval before rerun jobs finish launching.
Ensure automated workflow reruns launch once per run instead of repeating.
Hold back protection verification until all background rerun requests are dispatched.
search: The approval rerun workflow in .github/workflows/rerun-workflow-run.yml must deduplicate workflow run IDs and delay the protect job until all other reruns are submitted. Emitted rows format run IDs before job names to allow deduplication with sort -u -k1,1, preventing multiple reruns for runs with multiple failed jobs. Non-protect jobs run asynchronously in the background, requiring a wait command before submitting rerun $protect_id so protect does not fail against checks queued for rerun. Job names remain last in row formatting to accommodate spaces in job titles.
